These small empirical p95 values are not field statistics.

Two sequential actual Chrome captures after deployment: Riemann then EthLib, normal motion, 1440x960, no throttling, CDP tracing/CPU sampling. All seven served bundles match the hidden-map build byte-for-byte. No native perf sampler or concurrent validation process in these captures. Profiling/automation adds overhead.

Source is fetched once by the application and once by the profiler for its declaration/source-line oracle. Both requests occur in setup, not gesture phases. The initial host has no source publication, so no initial source fallback body is queried.

Synchronous EventDispatch excludes subsequent rendering. Input/two-rAF is a scheduling proxy, not physical presentation or field INP. Resize events can coalesce; p95 of eight/one samples is the maximum. Fit View and initial/same-node selection are separate from alternating-node clicks.

Native intervals overlap and must not be summed. Thread CPU excludes child workers; wall minus CPU is not an I/O-wait counter. Node counts decoded arrayBuffer body bytes; Playwright-reported responseBodySize is retained separately. Zero observations are unavailable, not measured zero work.

Node response p95 increased to about 42 ms for both projects despite lower native computation. Actual browser settled response p95 is 6.45 ms Riemann / 4.85 ms EthLib. Transport/client differences remain unattributed adapter measurements; this does not claim a universal HTTP response or rendering speedup.

Measurement hashes sort object keys, preserving arrays and decoded strings. They are comparison oracles, not authority or runtime cache identities. Raw original-source JSON, traces and source context remain under target/. No model/inference request is issued by the actual-project captures; both hosts remain unapproved.
